sections.h2: Which Oldham County office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
The sheriff's office sends the Oldham County tax bill, and the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) supplies the value behind it. The sheriff's tax collection page says one bill rolls up charges from the state, the county, the school districts, the city of Crestwood and 18 special districts. Mailing is finished by the end of September, and the sheriff's line is 502-222-9501.

A value that looks wrong is a PVA matter, at 502-222-9320. Each printed bill explains its due dates, the way to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage servicer pays for you.

sections.h2: What sets Oldham County apart from the rest of Kentucky?
sections.html:
Oldham County lies in north central Kentucky and belongs to the Louisville metropolitan area. Wikipedia's county profile ranks it first in the state for both wealth and education. Its 196 square miles make it the 13th smallest county in Kentucky, with the Ohio River marking the northern line against Indiana.

The legislature created it in 1823 from parts of Henry, Jefferson and Shelby counties. Towns sprouted along the Louisville and Frankfort railroad during the 1850s, and Interstate 71, completed in the early 1970s, tied the county to downtown Louisville. La Grange is the county seat and largest city. Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff are cities too, and Buckner and Westport are census-designated places.

Growth shows in the head count: 14,687 people in 1970, 27,795 in 1980, 43,455 in 1990, 60,316 in 2010 and 67,607 in 2020. Students attend Oldham County Schools, which operates North Oldham High School, Oldham County High School and South Oldham High School, and buyers often ask which of the three an address feeds.

sections.h2: How do the Oldham County numbers look?
sections.html:
Home values here sit far above the Kentucky norm. Survey figures in the table cover 2020 to 2024.

Mortgage holders carry median monthly costs of $2,193, while owners with no mortgage pay $712. Poverty touches 6.0 percent of residents. The county has 23,025 households of 2.84 people on average, and 17.1 percent of residents are 65 or older. At the 2020 census, 42.4 percent of households included children under 18, and the median age was 40.0.

sections.h2: When are Oldham County owners expected to pay?
sections.html:
Every Kentucky sheriff works from the same statewide calendar in KRS 134.015: a 2 percent discount through November 1, face value until the end of December, then penalties of 5 and later 10 percent.

  • Escrow customers should check that the lender paid before the discount deadline.
  • Fall closings need a clear answer from the title agent on who covers the current bill.
  • A Crestwood parcel carries the city's levy on the same bill as the county's.

Since the January 1 owner is the person on the hook for that year, a spring seller still receives the bill and divides it with the buyer when the sale closes.

sections.h2: How does an Oldham County owner argue against a valuation?
sections.html:
Phone the PVA and ask for a conference, the opening step in the process described by a statewide PVA appeal guide. Come with an opinion of value and the proof: sales of similar houses, an appraisal, repair quotes, or rent records.

No agreement means an appeal form at the Oldham County Clerk, then a local board of three residents, then the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, which wants a filing within 30 days of the mailed ruling. With homes at $393,100 in the middle of the market, comparable sales from the same subdivision are worth gathering carefully.

sections.h2: What does the clerk do with unpaid Oldham County bills?
sections.html:
On April 15, at the close of business, whatever the sheriff has not collected shifts to the County Clerk. The clerk's delinquent tax page in Oldham County points valuation questions to the PVA and tax sale rules to the state revenue department.

The state's collection guide lists the consequences: a lien on the parcel, 1 percent interest per month, notices mailed by the county attorney and a sale at least 90 days after the transfer. A certificate bought by an investor is then owed to the investor. An owner selling with a certificate open can pay it off from the closing proceeds after getting the clerk's quote.

sections.h2: What costs does an Oldham County seller face at closing?
sections.html:
The seller bears Kentucky's transfer tax, set at half a dollar per $500 of value (rounded up) and collected by the clerk alongside the deed (KRS 142.050). A $393,100 sale spans 787 units of $500 and so owes $393.50. Transfers between spouses, deeds that fix an earlier deed and foreclosure deeds are exempt.

  • The deed states the full price, both mailing addresses and where the next tax bill should go.
  • A gift, or a sale for token money, needs a sworn estimate of market value.
  • Heirs file an affidavit from the personal representative in every county where the estate owns land.

sections.h2: What is driving the Oldham County housing market?
sections.html:
Growth is steady. About 3,400 people joined the county from April 2020 to July 2025, builders took out 276 permits in 2025, and 46.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband reaches 95.4 percent of households, and a one-way commute averages 26.2 minutes.

The jobs picture explains the pull: the county had 1,404 employer establishments and 14,369 jobs in 2023, with $775.1 million in payroll, and stores rang up $728.0 million in sales in 2022. Health care and social assistance took in $350.7 million. About 74.8 percent of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census. Because the sheriff bills for 18 special districts as well as one city, two houses a few miles apart can pay different totals, so check the districts on a given bill before comparing listings.

faqs.q: Whom should I call about an Oldham County property value?
faqs.a: The PVA, 502-222-9320. Values come from that office, and the sheriff only collects what they produce.

faqs.q: When do Oldham County property tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: The sheriff's tax page says mailing wraps up by the end of September. Call 502-222-9501 if yours is missing in early October.

faqs.q: Is Crestwood's city tax billed separately?
faqs.a: No. The Crestwood levy rides on the same sheriff bill as the county and district charges, so a single payment covers all of them.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies to a median-priced Oldham County sale?
faqs.a: $393.50 on a $393,100 sale, paid by the seller to the clerk ahead of recording.

faqs.q: Can a house with a tax lien on it still be sold in Oldham County?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds.
